solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sponge transformed rugs once

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters of these two words, taken together

explanation.surface: Someone notes that old rugs have been turned into sponges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' reads as a noun for a cleaning item, but it is a verb: to live off others, which is SCROUNGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to cadge or freeload from other people, the same as to scrounge.

clue.text: Scrapping an Olympic sport

blocks.note: first meaning: quarrelling, having a row (rhyming with cow)
second meaning: propelling a boat with oars, raced at the Games

explanation.surface: An Olympic sport is being dropped from the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrapping' suggests abolishing, but here it means fighting; the two senses of the word are pronounced differently (row as in cow, row as in go).
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy argument, so rowing is squabbling; rowing is also the oar-powered boat racing contested at the Olympics.

clue.text: Smart black vase

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an urn is a large vase

explanation.surface: An elegant black vase, as described in a homeware catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like an adjective meaning stylish, but it is the verb: to sting or feel a burning pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that smarts gives a stinging pain, so to smart is to burn.

clue.text: Post first-class to reach Scottish island

blocks.note: a staff is a post or pole
A denotes first class, as in A1 or an A grade

explanation.surface: Mail sent first class so it can reach a remote Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is an uninhabited island off the west coast of Scotland, near Mull.

clue.text: Botanist may look thus on next page

blocks.note: first, whimsical meaning: a plant scientist would examine a leaf by peering over it
second meaning: on the other side of the sheet in a book

explanation.surface: A reader's note pointing to a botanical illustration on the following page.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading of the word split in two, over a leaf; the second is its ordinary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse side of the page, so continuing on the next page.

clue.text: Displays suede pants — around five pairs?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or poor, so the word before it is badly arranged
around says the scrambled word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
five pairs make ten, which is X in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fashion remark about someone wearing suede trousers, wondering if they own five pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers (in British English, underwear) but works as slang for 'rubbish'. The jumbled suede is split as E...UDES around the ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To exude is to give off or show plainly, as one exudes confidence, so it means displays.

clue.text: Up in Rhyl, Noel's alone

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the end of the town name and the start of the man's name

explanation.surface: A man called Noel is on his own up in Rhyl, a seaside town in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and alone both mean single, with no one else, as in an only child.

clue.text: Councillor, old and restful, avoiding one game on lawn

indicators.note: avoiding says a letter is kept out of the word it governs

blocks.note: Cllr or CR is an abbreviation for councillor
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a restful place is a quiet one
I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: An elderly councillor relaxing but steering clear of a lawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: Croquet is played on a lawn, knocking wooden balls through hoops with mallets.

clue.text: Bad-tempered woman, former spouse recalled, into French wine

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling something back, so the letters run backwards
into says one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A grumpy woman remembering her ex while drinking French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen is a female fox, and by extension a quarrelsome, shrewish woman.

clue.text: Group of stars having duck and port with knight

blocks.note: a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A celebrity group dining on duck with a glass of port, alongside a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of stars' hints at famous people, but it is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion, the hunter, is a prominent constellation, which is a pattern of stars.

clue.text: Famous scientist dreamy, wanting diamonds for wife

indicators.note: wanting one thing for another means the first takes the place of the second

blocks.note: a dreamy look is a faraway one
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds
W is the standard abbreviation for wife, the letter replaced

explanation.surface: A distracted scientist who would rather have jewels than a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The single W in the word for dreamy is swapped for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Faraday was the English physicist and chemist known for his work on electromagnetism.

clue.text: Place for valuables close, turning key fast

indicators.note: turning things over mixes up their order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
E is a musical key
taken as written, mixed in with the key

explanation.surface: Somewhere to keep valuables locked, the key turned quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'turning' look like part of a lock picture, but key is a musical note joining fast in the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A night safe is a bank's slot in an outside wall where valuables can be deposited out of hours.

clue.text: Group of workers with Royal Navy support retreat

blocks.note: TU is a trade union, a group of workers
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Union workers and the navy backing a military withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn back is to reverse course and go back, which is what retreating is.

clue.text: Health centre son joined with father

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A son and his father going to a health club together.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a resort or centre offering health treatments, originally at mineral springs.

clue.text: Deacon broadcast both sides of the short story

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order
both sides of points to the outer letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first and last letters of this little word

explanation.surface: A church deacon telling a short story on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a brief, often amusing account of a real incident, so a short story.

clue.text: Regularly tell off mischievous child?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A parent wonders whether to scold a naughty child yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Elf is used of a small, impish child, after the mischievous sprites of folklore.

clue.text: Reportedly stabilise architectural adornment

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so we want a word that sounds like the one defined next

blocks.note: to freeze prices is to stabilise them

explanation.surface: A report about shoring up a decorative carving on a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a horizontal band of sculpted or painted decoration along a wall.

clue.text: Put restrictions on gang criminal

blocks.note: a ring is a gang of criminals, as in a smuggling ring
a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Authorities clamp down on a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as an adjective but is a noun here, a handler of stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money or land is to restrict its use to one purpose, protecting it from others.

clue.text: Most modern members of flock probing religious books

indicators.note: probing means pushing inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: ewes are female sheep, members of a flock
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: The latest flock members nosing into some holy books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' hints at a congregation, matching religious books, but it is sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest is the superlative of new, so the most recent or most modern.

clue.text: Person who steals a pound

blocks.note: first meaning: one who nicks, British slang for stealing
second meaning: British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.surface: A thief who takes a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to nick is to steal, and a nicker is a pound coin or note.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicker is literally someone who nicks or steals, and the same word is slang for a pound.

clue.text: Weather feature depicted by artist in East London area

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
Bow is a district in the East End of London

explanation.surface: A painter capturing a weather scene in the East End.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is an arc of colours formed when sunlight shines through rain, a weather phenomenon.

clue.text: Sheets of paper, yellowish-white, Charlie removed

indicators.note: removed says a letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: cream is a pale yellowish-white colour
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A stack of off-white paper from which someone named Charlie has been removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, 500 sheets.

clue.text: One in road moved fast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: an ace is a one in cards
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A single car on the road sped along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' suggests I or A, but here it is the ace, the one in a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to move or go at high speed, so raced means moved fast.

clue.text: Fleece covering English gown

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece covering another sits on top of it, so it comes first

blocks.note: to fleece someone is to rob or swindle them
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A sheepskin worn over an English gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a woolly garment fitting the clothing theme, but it is the verb to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose outer garment, the same as a gown.

clue.text: Article, current, on unknown Antipodean soldier

indicators.note: in an across entry, one piece placed on another comes after it

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
Z is an unknown quantity in algebra
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A reference to an unknown Australian or New Zealand soldier, like the unknown warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: Anzac comes from Australian and New Zealand Army Corps; Antipodean means from Australia or New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anzac is a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps of the First World War.

clue.text: Citizen's aquatic vessel caught in stream

indicators.note: in places the preceding piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a sub is a submarine, an underwater vessel
a jet is a stream of liquid or gas
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A citizen's boat stuck in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' does two jobs: it gives C and says where it goes, inside the stream word.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is a member of a state owing allegiance to a monarch, so a citizen.
